Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’ll first read the workspace contract and the wake-visual inspection skill, then inspect the current/inherited evidence before changing any policy. I’ll keep the ablation boundary strict and produce one candidate only.

The visual-first skill requires anchoring images to observations and metrics, then comparing the best finite run with the most informative failure. I’m applying that sequence now; no policy edits will happen until the visual diagnosis and hypothesis are written.

The visual evidence shows the same developed staggered wakes at release. The `0.75` anchor turns into the target on a compact diagonal arc; the `0.77` sample takes a deeper, more horizontal final approach, while the inherited rate-feedback variant overshoots below the direct corridor and carries much higher force/moment load. I’m now isolating the exact controller differences before choosing the single probe.

The inherited `0.745` lower-side probe is now evaluated—and it falsifies the prior interpolation hypothesis. Two behaviorally identical rollouts slowed capture to `86.99`, reduced upstream-relative speed to `0.05865`, and raised RMS force/moment to `39.84/540.72`; visually, they overshoot below the compact corridor. I’m recording that negative lesson and will keep the proven `0.75` steering law fixed while isolating a small action-guard probe.

The candidate now changes only the soft acceleration guard from `28` to `29 rad/time²`, retaining the evaluated steering and gait. The notes and durable negative lesson are in place; I’m running the mandated guidance, policy-contract, and boundary checks separately, with no CFD rollout.

The guidance check passed. The policy check did not start because this environment’s login shell cannot find `julia` (and emitted unrelated SSH-profile errors); I’m resolving the local executable path without changing the candidate, then I’ll rerun the same check.

All mandated checks now pass: durable-guidance validation, Julia policy contract, and editable-boundary enforcement. I’m doing a final scope audit to confirm there is one non-empty candidate and only the intended policy delta.

Completed one 2D multi-wake candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl): retains the proven steering/gait and probes `acceleration_limit=29.0`.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md): records visual diagnosis and falsifiable hypothesis.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md): materially revised with the negative `0.745` interpolation result.

Guidance validation, Julia policy-contract check, and boundary check all pass. No CFD was run.
